text:
fiona: Post-RFC follow-up question: should the fallback decision be cached for a short window to avoid thrash if detector flaps? Draft idea: decision_cache_ttl_s per-service, default 60s. Thoughts?

marc: Yes. If detectors are noisy we can end up switching back and forth. Cache + a cool-down state machine works well: cached decision -> cooldown until TTL expires, ignore new identical triggers.

liam: Agree but we need to be careful with signal drift. Cache key should include route+service+target_model so a different target still evaluates. Also expose cache_hit metric: fallback.cache.hit and fallback.cache.miss.

fiona: Good point. Cache key: service|route|decision_type|target_version. We'll emit fallback.cache.hit/miss and fallback.cache.evictions.

marc: Backpressure: when control plane is overloaded (high decision latency) we should prefer noop or drain instead of immediate switch. Proposal: decision_score float in payload, and policy that applies threshold tiers.

liam: Can we make the decision API return a recommended hold-back window if overloaded, e.g. "recommended_cooldown_s": 300? Ops can then respect it. Also include decision_id and evaluated_at in response.

fiona: Sounds useful. API sketch: POST /internal/v1/decisions with body (flat keys only): service, route, detector_id, trigger_ts, signals_map_encoded, suggested_action, target, decision_id (optional client-provided). Response: decision_id, evaluated_at, applied_action, recommended_cooldown_s.

marc: For durability, decisions should be logged to a decisions stream (append-only) and processed idempotently. If clients re-send with same decision_id, the stream should ignore duplicates.

liam: Canary escape hatch: when rolling back to previous model we should allow a progressive canary that steps: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with configurable step_delay_s. The decision event should include canary_steps CSV and step_delay_s.

fiona: Example decision payload (ops friendly):
```json
{"service":"api","route":"/v1/generate","detector_id":"det-42","trigger_ts":4100001234,"signals":"latency_p95=1200;err_pct=2.3;model_quality_delta=-0.04","suggested_action":"switch","target":"model-2026-04-01","decision_id":"dec-4100001234-01"}
```

marc: Nice. Note: signals encoded as semicolon pairs to keep flat structure. Emphasize no raw request bodies; include request_hash only.

liam: Alert rules: page infra if fallback.decisions.applied_action == "abort" and aborts_in_10m > 2. Also page if decision_latency_ms > 2000 repeatedly.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary policy tweak applied to staging: canary_steps="5,20,50,100" step_delay_s=180.

fiona: One more ops note: add a manual override endpoint for quick escape: POST /ops/decisions/{decision_id}/override {action:"pin"|"force-switch"|"cancel"} with authorization audit. Include snippet in runbook.

liam: I'll add emitter tests for cache metrics and ensure metric names are stable. marc, can you own the decisions stream retention policy?

marc: Yep, will propose 30d retention and index by decision_id and provenance.

fiona: Great. I'll update the runbook with cache_ttl default 60s, recommended_cooldown usage, canary_steps, and the override snippet. PR incoming. :rocket:
